hero.headline: Friday.
hero.description: A desktop AI assistant for macOS. Summon it with Option Space, ask for help, and get back to what you were doing.

demoSuggestions.answer: Hey Maya, thanks so much for the invite. I cannot make Thursday, but I would love to find another time. Want me to send a few options for next week?

landingFeatures.title: Anywhere on macOS
landingFeatures.description: Summon Friday from the desktop and keep the current task in view. Files, tools, voice, and workspace context stay close without another browser tab.

landingFeatures.title: Remembers, without hiding the record
landingFeatures.description: Local stores keep useful context such as settings, skills, schedules, channels, and session state inspectable and deletable.

landingFeatures.title: Desktop, not another tab
landingFeatures.description: Friday is built around desktop work: files, terminal commands, local settings, provider keys, and approval checks remain visible.

landingFeatures.title: Your choice of model
landingFeatures.description: Route chat, voice, images, research, and realtime work through configured providers instead of being locked into one model.

landingFeatures.title: Scriptable workflows
landingFeatures.description: Turn repeated tasks into skills, scheduled prompts, connector actions, or channel deliveries with clear permission boundaries.

landingFeatures.title: Honest about uncertainty
landingFeatures.description: Friday can ask before acting, surface run state, and keep private workspace data under user control instead of pretending every action is safe.

faqs.question: Does Friday send my data anywhere?
faqs.answer: Friday is local-first. Data leaves your machine only when you direct it to: calling an AI provider, syncing a connector, posting to a channel, or running a hosted service. API keys, workspace paths, and chat history stay local.

faqs.question: Can I use a local or self-hosted model?
faqs.answer: Yes. Friday supports any provider with an OpenAI-compatible endpoint — including locally hosted models. Configure a base URL and API key in provider settings to route the agent to your own runtime.

faqs.question: How does the tool approval system work?
faqs.answer: Each connector and tool has a configurable approval policy — always require approval, skip approval for a specific allowed-tool list, or never require approval. Pre-run safety hooks evaluate the prompt before the provider is ever called.

faqs.question: Can I choose different AI providers for different tasks?
faqs.answer: Yes. Configure separate providers for the main assistant, speech-to-text, text-to-speech, image creation, video creation, and music creation. Each operator resolves its own provider and model from your stored settings.

faqs.question: How do scheduled tasks work?
faqs.answer: The cron scheduler supports cron expressions, fixed intervals, and one-time runs — all timezone-aware. Missed-run policies control what happens on startup if a run was skipped. Concurrency policies control what happens when a new run fires while one is still active.

faqs.question: What messaging channels does Friday support?
faqs.answer: Friday has a catalog of 22 channels including Telegram (the only bundled runtime), Slack, Discord, WhatsApp, iMessage, Microsoft Teams, Signal, Matrix, LINE, Feishu, IRC, Twitch, Nextcloud Talk, Nostr, QQ Bot, and more. Each channel can have per-account allow-lists and DM policies.

faqs.question: How does context memory work across sessions?
faqs.answer: Friday uses startup files — AGENTS.md, SOUL.md, IDENTITY.md, USER.md, MEMORY.md, and others — as lower-priority project context injected into every prompt. When a session grows too long, the transcript is automatically compacted: the six most recent entries are kept verbatim and older entries are summarised.

faqs.question: Will it work on Intel Macs?
faqs.answer: The current target is macOS 13+. Final packaging details for Apple Silicon vs. Intel should be verified against the release artifacts.

privacyNotes: Friday is local-first but can connect to external AI providers, channels, apps, and connectors.
API keys, tokens, passwords, private keys, and credentials are secrets and should not be logged or exposed.
Provider keys are stored locally and only used for provider calls.
Chat history, workspace paths, channel IDs, connector metadata, local files, and agent data are treated as private.
Users can inspect chat history size and clear the active conversation history.
Application data and user data folders can be opened from settings.
App settings include theme, language, translucency, menu bar visibility, keep-awake behavior, and microphone control.
Tool and connector actions that write, delete, publish, or access private data should pass permission checks.
